title: Data on THMs concentration and spatial trend in water distribution network (a preliminary study in center of Iran)
author: Mohammadi, Ebrahimi, et al.
materials: Sampling procedure was carried out in the autumn and winter seasons 2017, 30 samples were taken from water distribution network during each season, according to standard methods for water and wastewater examination [6]. Prior to the sampling, bottles (300-mL amber glass) were washed using detergent–deionized water, and then dried in an oven at 400 °C. Furthermore, sodium thiosulfate was added to the sampling bottles for removal of disinfection chlorine and inhibition of THMs formation during samples transportation and storage. Sampling process was done in official and commercial buildings using tap water. The main advantages of THMs spatial mapping are classified color and easy optical detection. The THMs concentrations in the red area were higher than those in the yellow area. Thus, this protocol could be easily used for reporting of quality and quantity THMs in water distribution network. Furthermore, the application of the data and graphical report can be very interesting.

steps.title: Prepare sampling bottles
steps.instruction: Clean 300 mL amber glass bottles, add sodium thiosulfate, and dry them before sampling.

substeps.instruction: Wash each bottle with detergent followed by de‑ionized water.
Dry bottles in an oven set to 400 °C.
Add sodium thiosulfate to each bottle to quench chlorine and inhibit THM formation.

steps.title: Collect water samples and field data
steps.instruction: Take tap‑water samples and record pH, EC, residual chlorine, and temperature at each site.

substeps.instruction: In autumn and winter 2017, collect 30 samples per season from official and commercial buildings using the prepared bottles.
Measure pH with a pH meter 310 AUTECH, electrical conductivity (EC) with the appropriate meter, and residual chlorine with a chlorine meter model 5f8700‑12 HACH.
Record the water temperature at the sampling point (autumn 23 ± 2 °C, winter 14 ± 2 °C).

steps.title: Analyze samples by GC/MS
steps.instruction: Run each sample on a GC/MS system using specified column and injector settings, and accept results meeting quality criteria.

substeps.instruction: Install a DB5‑MS capillary column (30 m length, 0.25 mm internal diameter).
Set the injector to split mode, temperature 160 °C, and inject 1500 μL headspace from a 10 cc sample.
Use helium as carrier gas at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Analyze each sample and its blank in duplicate.
Accept results only if the relative standard deviation (RSD) is <30 %.
Confirm recoveries of the standard reference compound and external standards are between 91.6 % and 95.2 %.
Note that the method detection limit is 0.5 μg/L.

steps.title: Create THM distribution maps
steps.instruction: Use ArcGIS to interpolate and visualize THM concentrations for each season.

substeps.instruction: Import the measured THM concentrations into ArcGIS.
Apply the Kriging interpolation method to generate independent raster layers for each THM.
Evaluate the Kriging model by confirming % RMSE is greater than 40 %.
Use the raster calculator to overlay the individual THM layers and produce seasonal maps.
Apply a multi‑dimensional stretch style to highlight high‑THM (red) and low‑THM (yellow) areas.

steps.title: Reference THM guideline limits
steps.instruction: Record the regulatory limits for total THMs for comparison with measured values.

substeps.instruction: World Health Organization (WHO) guideline: total THMs ≤ 1 (unit as in the study).
U.S. EPA guideline: total THMs ≤ 80 μg/L.
